# Results — Study 595 (Managed-Futures Sleeve)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **carving
10-20% of a 60/40 portfolio into a managed-futures (trend-following) sleeve improves it:
near-zero correlation plus 2022-style crisis alpha** — tested on a simple 12-month TSMOM
replication book over the desk's shared 18-contract futures panel, blended with a monthly-
rebalanced SPY/VBMFX 60/40, plus the live one-ticket ETFs (DBMF, KMLM). Siblings
[31-trade-winds](../../31-trade-winds/) and [518-time-series-momentum](../../518-time-series-momentum/)
graded the STANDALONE trend premium **Weak**; that verdict is cited, not re-litigated — the
unit under test here is the **portfolio improvement**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-07-03**: the joint
replication window ends **2026-05-31** (the shared futures tape stops 2026-06-11, so the
partial June is dropped); the live-ETF window ends **2026-06-30** (June complete on the ETF
tape). Fingerprint `2f0e9858dde3` (joint monthly panel; futures-monthly `b1cdf7bc6129`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Futures | shared `_cache/trade_winds_futures.parquet` — 18 continuous contracts (equity/rates/commodity/FX), 6,547 days, 2000-07-18 → 2026-06-11 |
| ETFs / rf | yfinance total-return closes: SPY + VBMFX (1999-01-04 → 2026-06-30), DBMF (2019-05-08 →), KMLM (2020-12-02 →); ^IRX 13-week T-bill yield = the risk-free leg |
| Joint window | **2001-09-30 → 2026-05-31** (297 months) |
| Sleeve | 12-mo TSMOM: sign of trailing 12-month return, 40%/σ inverse-vol per contract / N, monthly rebalance; avg gross leverage **3.71×**, avg turnover **1.12× NAV/mo** |
| Execution / costs | exactly **one month** of lag (signal & vol through month-end t-1, held month t); **5 bps one-way × traded notional** headline (2/10 shown); futures shorts post margin and pay **no borrow**; the blended sleeve is cash-collateralised (rf + excess) and pays the **0.85%/yr** live-ETF fee; Sharpe races are **excess-vs-excess** |

> **Panel caveats (named on the Signal axis).** The 18 contracts are liquid futures *still
> trading in 2026* — mild survivorship (TSMOM shorts a faller rather than deleting it, so the
> bias is far weaker than an equity sort, but it is named). The continuous series are
> yfinance front-month splices, inheriting study 31's roll construction. The replication book
> is gross of real-world slippage beyond the modeled bps (its +33% in 2022 vs DBMF's +21.6%
> live shows the flattering gap).

## Axis 1a — "near-zero correlation": decisively real

| pair | corr | 95% CI (Fisher-z) | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **MF book vs 60/40** | **−0.054** | **[−0.167, +0.060]** | 297 |
| MF book vs stocks (SPY excess) | −0.053 | [−0.166, +0.061] | 297 |
| MF book vs bonds (VBMFX excess) | −0.021 | [−0.135, +0.093] | 297 |
| DBMF vs 60/40 (live) | −0.212 | [−0.408, +0.002] | 84 |
| KMLM vs 60/40 (live) | −0.432 | [−0.611, −0.210] | 65 |

The diversification half of the pitch is **not folklore**: 25 years of replication put the
correlation within ±0.17 of zero, and the live wrappers run outright *negative*. DBMF tracks
the replication book at **+0.682** [+0.547, +0.783] — the ETF is the same animal.

## Axis 1b — the improvement: positive everywhere, certified nowhere

60/40 (monthly-rebalanced SPY/VBMFX) vs 85% 60/40 + 15% cash-collateralised sleeve
(net of 5 bps futures costs **and** the 0.85%/yr ETF fee), 297 months:

| portfolio | CAGR | vol | Sharpe (excess) | maxDD | MAR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 60/40 | 7.52% | 9.37% | 0.643 | −32.4% | 0.232 |
| **+15% sleeve** | **7.72%** | **8.29%** | **0.738** | **−23.4%** | **0.330** |

| test of the improvement | value |
|---|--:|
| MF alpha vs 60/40 (NW, 6 lags) | **+8.13%/yr · t = +2.10** (β = −0.107, R² = 0.3%) |
| ΔSharpe (blend − 60/40) | **+0.095** |
| block-bootstrap 95% CI (5,000 draws, block 6, paired rows) | **[−0.064, +0.242]** · one-sided p = **0.119** |

The point estimates all move the right way — Sharpe +0.10, drawdown cut by 9 points, MAR
+42% — and the mean-variance criterion (the sleeve's alpha on the 60/40) clears the bar at
**t = 2.10** *at the headline config*. But the direct bootstrap of the claimed quantity
(ΔSharpe) **never excludes zero**, and the alpha t is fragile (below):
**Real on the correlation · Weak on the certified improvement → Signal = MIXED.**

## Robustness — where the t breaks

| knob | result |
|---|---|
| sleeve size | 10%: ΔS +0.070, CI [−0.031, +0.162], p 0.080 · **15%: +0.095, [−0.064, +0.242], p 0.119** · 20%: +0.110, [−0.111, +0.317], p 0.164 |
| one-way cost | 2 bps: alpha t **+2.20** · 5 bps: **+2.10** · 10 bps: **+1.92** |
| lookback | 9m: book Sharpe 0.209, alpha t **+1.35**, ΔS +0.045 · **12m: 0.407, +2.10, +0.095** · 15m: 0.352, **+1.67**, +0.060 |
| NW lags (12m, 5bps) | 3: t +2.06 · 6: +2.10 · 12: +2.25 |
| sub-periods (ΔSharpe of the 15% blend) | 2001-09→2008-12: **+0.257** · 2009-01→2019-12: **−0.107** · 2020-01→2026-05: **+0.147** |

Only the canonical 12-month lookback at ≤5 bps clears t = 2; its 9- and 15-month neighbours
sit at 1.35 and 1.67. And the benefit is **regime-dependent**: the sleeve *dragged* on the
blend for the entire 2009-2019 QE decade (ΔSharpe −0.107) — eleven years of paying insurance
premium with no fire.

## 2022 — the crisis-alpha year (calendar total returns)

| leg | 2022 |
|---|--:|
| SPY | −18.18% |
| VBMFX (bonds) | −13.24% |
| 60/40 | −15.91% |
| MF sleeve (replication, funded, net) | **+33.13%** |
| **60/40 + 15% sleeve** | **−9.02%** |
| DBMF (live, net of fee) | +21.60% |
| KMLM (live, net of fee) | +24.24% |

The sleeve contributed **~+5.0 pp** to the blend in the one year both halves of the 60/40
fell together — the crisis-alpha half of the pitch happened, live and on the tape (a single
descriptive year, no significance test possible).

## Third axis — is the benefit just bonds in disguise? **BUSTED**

| test | value |
|---|--:|
| corr(MF, bonds), 297 mo | **−0.021** [−0.135, +0.093] · β on bonds −0.093 · R² **0.0%** |
| 2022: bonds vs sleeve | **−13.24% vs +33.13%** — opposite signs in the one year it mattered |
| shift the same 15 pts into bonds (45/55) instead | Sharpe 0.664 · maxDD −24.1% · 2022 **−15.15%** |
| vs the 15% sleeve blend | Sharpe **0.738** · maxDD −23.4% · 2022 **−9.02%** |

The sleeve carries **zero bond loading** (R² rounds to 0.0%), and in the rising-rate crash —
exactly where a bonds-in-disguise sleeve would have died — it was **short** bonds and paid.
More bonds would have made 2022 *worse*.

## Live ETF check — DBMF/KMLM (2019-07 → 2026-06, 84 months; descriptive)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| DBMF net-of-fee | CAGR 8.85% · vol 11.4% · Sharpe 0.562 · maxDD −17.3% |
| 60/40 → +15% DBMF | Sharpe 0.671 → **0.790** · maxDD −20.1% → **−13.5%** |
| live ΔSharpe | **+0.119** · CI [−0.048, +0.279] · p 0.090 |

The live wrappers reproduce the replication's story — negative correlation, real 2022 payoff,
a positive-but-uncertified Sharpe improvement — on 7 years of net-of-fee tape.

## Random-sign placebo — the improvement is not diversification arithmetic

Same sizing, lag, costs and fee, with the trend sign replaced by an iid coin, averaged over
**24 seeds**: mean placebo book Sharpe **−0.230** (sd 0.197), mean placebo ΔSharpe
**−0.0772** (sd 0.0448). A zero-edge uncorrelated sleeve *hurts* the blend — the observed
+0.095 needs the trend signal, not just "any low-correlation thing".

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

Joint (stock, bond, MF) world, 312 months, corr 0, fee charged, planted MF Sharpe as knob:

| planted MF Sharpe | ΔSharpe | 95% CI | p | alpha NW t |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (null) | −0.026 | [−0.106, +0.062] | 0.697 | +0.00 |
| 0.8 | +0.156 | [+0.077, +0.246] | 0.000 | +4.45 |

The ΔSharpe bootstrap and the alpha t stay quiet on a zero-edge sleeve and light up on a
planted one. *(Machinery proof only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** *(Real on the correlation · Weak on the certified improvement)*. The
  "near-zero correlation" half is decisively real: −0.054 [−0.167, +0.060] over 297 months,
  and the live ETFs run negative (DBMF −0.212, KMLM −0.432). The improvement half points the
  right way everywhere (Sharpe 0.643 → 0.738, maxDD −32.4% → −23.4%, alpha t = 2.10 at the
  headline config) but the bootstrap ΔSharpe CI **spans zero** at every sleeve size and the
  alpha t collapses to 1.35-1.92 across neighbouring lookbacks and costs — a t ≥ 2 that
  survives only at the snoopable canonical config is not a certified improvement. Mild
  futures-panel survivorship named.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Genuinely accessible (DBMF/KMLM are one-ticket, liquid,
  0.85-0.90% ER wrappers; the fee is charged in every headline number and the live window
  shows the same improvement net of it) — but the benefit is regime-dependent: an entire
  2009-2019 decade of negative carry on the blend, and the certified edge is absent. You can
  buy it cheaply; the tape cannot promise it pays.
- **"Just bonds in disguise?" — BUSTED.** Zero bond loading (corr −0.021, R² 0.0%); in 2022
  bonds lost −13.24% while the sleeve made +33.13% (DBMF +21.60% live); shifting the same 15
  points into bonds gives a worse Sharpe (0.664 vs 0.738) and no 2022 protection (−15.15% vs
  −9.02%). The sleeve is its own asset — it is *not* leveraged duration.
